questions.question: An approved helmet:

options.text: Lets you see as far to the sides as you need for safe riding.
Does not have a chin strap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lets you see as far to the sides as you need for safe riding.
questions.explanation: Some people think a helmet limits your vision, but this is not true. Any DOT-approved helmet lets you see as far as you need for safe riding.

questions.question: Low-speed crashes:

options.text: Happen frequently, so you do not need to worry about them.

questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen at speeds below 30 miles per hour. Even low-speed crashes can be fatal.

questions.question: Head and neck injuries can be reduced by:
questions.explanation: Wearing a good-quality helmet greatly reduces the risk of head and neck injuries. A helmet is your best protection in a crash.

questions.question: The shortest and safest stops happen when you:

options.text: Use both the front and rear brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: Use both the front and rear brakes smoothly and gradually to stop safely and quickly. Do not lock up either tire.

questions.question: The best gear to wear while riding is:

options.text: Any gear that helps protect you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Any gear that helps protect you.
questions.explanation: Wear gear that protects you while riding. Wear a DOT-approved helmet, eye or face protection, and protective clothing.

questions.question: When checking tire pressure:

options.text: Looking at the tire is a good enough method.
Squeeze the tire to check it.
Compare the tire height to another tire.

questions.explanation: Use a tire gauge to check pressure before every ride. A tire that looks fine may actually be under-inflated, so looking at it is not enough.

questions.question: Motorcycle signals are:

options.text: Even more important than signals on cars and trucks.
Only needed when another vehicle is right next to you.
Less important than signals on cars and trucks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Even more important than signals on cars and trucks.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle riders are more vulnerable than car and truck drivers. Because of this, using signals is even more important for motorcycle riders.

questions.question: When following a car, you should:

options.text: Ride where the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
Ride next to another car to be more visible.
Stay on the left side of your lane.
Stay on the right side of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride where the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Position yourself so the driver can see you in their rearview mirror. Riding in the center of the lane is best because the driver is most likely to see you there.

questions.question: A plastic face shield protects you from:
questions.explanation: A face shield protects you from wind, dust, dirt, rain, insects, and pebbles. It also protects your face during a crash.

questions.question: For good protection, riding pants should:

options.text: Fit loose enough to flap in the wind.
Be short and expose your legs.

questions.explanation: Wear pants made of leather or strong synthetic material that cover your entire legs. Pants should fit snug but not so tight that they limit your movement.

questions.question: Keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles helps you:

options.text: Have time to react if another driver makes a mistake.
Stay in one area of the lane with limited movement.
Depend on others to spot hazards.
Go faster to stay with traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have time to react if another driver makes a mistake.
questions.explanation: Space around your motorcycle gives you time and room to react if another driver makes a mistake.

questions.question: If your front tire goes flat, what happens?

options.text: The back of the motorcycle will jerk side to side.

questions.explanation: A flat front tire makes steering feel heavy and is very dangerous because it affects your ability to steer.

questions.question: You drink four typical alcoholic drinks. After two hours, how many drinks are left in your body at minimum?
questions.explanation: Your body eliminates about one drink per hour. So after two hours, at least two drinks remain in your system.

questions.question: When should you use a turn signal?

options.text: When you plan to increase your speed.
Only when there is heavy traffic.

questions.explanation: Use a turn signal every time you turn or change lanes, even if no one seems to be around.

questions.question: What is the only way to remove alcohol from your body?
questions.explanation: Only time can remove alcohol from your body. There are no shortcuts to sobering up.

questions.question: What is the single most effective thing you can do to survive an accident?
questions.explanation: Wearing a helmet is the most important thing you can do to reduce injury or death in an accident.

questions.question: What is the best source of information about your motorcycle?

options.text: Someone who rides a different type of motorcycle.
A television show about motorcycle riding.

questions.explanation: Read the owner's manual before riding your motorcycle for the first time. This is especially important if you are riding a borrowed motorcycle.

questions.question: During the day, you should:

options.text: Not ride with your headlight on.
Ride with your headlight on only if it is cloudy.
Always ride with your headlight on.
Use your headlight only if you think it helps.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always ride with your headlight on.
questions.explanation: Always keep your headlight on when riding, even during the day. This makes you twice as likely to be noticed by other drivers.

questions.question: Wearing a helmet will:

options.text: Reduce your chances of head and neck injuries in a crash.
Increase your chances of a neck injury in a crash.
Not affect your chances of a head injury in a crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your chances of head and neck injuries in a crash.
questions.explanation: An approved helmet reduces the risk of head and neck injuries in a crash. An approved helmet will not limit your vision for safe riding.

questions.question: Keeping space around your motorcycle:

options.text: Is only necessary for beginning riders.
Gives you time and space to react to hazards.
Allows you to weave through traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gives you time and space to react to hazards.
questions.explanation: Keep your distance from other vehicles. Space around your motorcycle gives you time and room to maneuver around danger.
